title: Control Plane Workbench: Standup Notes and Triage - 2026-11-30
body:
Context and goal:
This was a longer-than-usual standup that functioned as a workbench: quick sync + focused triage on two signal paths causing recent client-facing latency spikes (routing fallthroughs) and an auth token renewal race that surfaced quota exhaustion symptoms. The aim was to capture immediate mitigations, clarify who owns follow-ups, and sketch experiments to avoid recurrence.

Attendance quick notes (rapid round-robin):
- Maya: running a short sampling job on route-assignment latencies; saw 2% of requests taking a fallback path with TTL > 600ms.
- Ethan: isolated metric bump in the auth layer; token refresh queue depth correlated with quota backend timeouts.
- Lena: working on new instrumentation for per-route KV-cache hit rates; found a handful of routes with <20% prefix cache reuse.
- Samir: prepping a canary for the allocator change; wants one more run with throttled burst to confirm backpressure behavior.
- Jules: cruise control on rollout pipeline; flagged an RBAC edge where service account migrations will hit the quota path.

Observed symptoms and immediate hypotheses:
1) Routing fallthrough burst (late-Nov window)
   - Symptom: transient spike in requests routed to regional fallback model cluster instead of hot pool; users saw 300-800ms additional latency.
   - Hypothesis: allocator heuristics misprioritized routing keys for traffic patterns with many short-lived sessions; KV cache misses amplified effect.
   - Quick evidence: sampler traces show suffix of call sequence where routing table read returned stale capacity tokens; the allocator then issued a slow path that triggers fallback.

2) Auth renewal backlog + quota thrashing
   - Symptom: auth-token-renew job experienced increasing retry loops causing downstream rate-limited calls into KMS/quota service; observed 429s from quota service.
   - Hypothesis: simultaneous migration of a service account changed token TTL semantics and increased renew frequency; retry policy compounded problem.
   - Quick evidence: timeline lines up with Jenkins job that rotated keys for staging clusters and a mismatch in TTL-leading flags in the client library.

Decisions and immediate mitigations (what we did in-standup)
- Short-circuit routing fallthrough: turned on temporary stricter affinity rule for hot-pool selection for 2 hours to reduce fallback pressure. (Owner: Maya; status: done at 11:15 UTC)
- Auth backoff adjustment: increased jitter and exponent cap on token-renew retries to reduce thundering herd. (Owner: Ethan; status: deployed to staging 11:40 UTC)
- Emergency quota throttle: added a soft limiter that rejects high-burst background renewals with circuit-breaker until library patch is out. (Owner: Jules; status: toggled on)

Follow-ups and experiments (next 2 weeks)
- Experiment A: allocator simulation with session churn
  - Goal: reproduce path that caused hot-pool misassignment under synthetic short-session workload.
  - How: run allocator sim with churn profile (p95 session length 4s, burst 20k/s) and collect route token freshness metrics.
  - Owner: Samir; Due: 2026-12-07

- Experiment B: KV-cache warmup heuristic tweak
  - Goal: bias prefix caching toward routes with high short-sequence reuse for first 30s of session to reduce cold misses.
  - How: implement configurable TTL boost and run A/B on 10% traffic in dev region.
  - Owner: Lena; Due: 2026-12-05 (dev), rollout decision 2026-12-10

- Investigation C: token TTL mismatch audit across SDKs
  - Goal: find client libs with inconsistent TTL flags after recent service-account tooling change.
  - How: grep for token-renew semantics, run synthetic renew spikes per-sdk, produce a remediation checklist.
  - Owner: Ethan + Maya; Due: 2026-12-03

Operational notes and logs to attach:
- Collected trace IDs: trace-2026-11-29-AB12, trace-2026-11-29-CD34 (attached to JIRA PLT-4821).
- Added temporary alert: cp.routing.fallback-rate (>0.5% sustained for 5m) -> Pager. (Owner: Jules)
- Added a dashboard tile for auth.renew.retry-depth by service account (quickview). (Owner: Ethan)

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the allocator serve stale capacity tokens? Need to confirm whether it was a race during concurrent topology updates or missed invalidation signals. (Samir to prioritize log correlation)
- Are there other service accounts with the rotated TTL behavior? We suspect at least two internal ones used by ingestion pipelines. (Ethan to audit)
- Long tail: is there a systemic interaction between prefix caching policy and the allocator algorithm that increases fallback risk when session churn is high? (Lena + Samir to prototype)

Action item tracker (brief)
- PLT-4821: primary issue ticket for routing fallback (assignee: Samir)
- PLT-4822: SDK TTL audit and hotfix (assignee: Ethan)
- PLT-4823: KV-cache heuristic POC (assignee: Lena)
- PLT-4824: Thundering-herd postmortem doc (assignee: Maya)

Quick retrospective notes from the standup
- Communication: the incident surfaced across SRE, serving runtime, and auth teams; cross-team channel helped but we should refine the incident escalation path for multi-subsystem partial degradations.
- Observability: we need per-request handoff tracing between allocator -> route table -> auth client to reduce friction during diagnosis. Low-friction traces would have cut triage time by ~30%.
- Rollouts: consider a preflight simulation gate for allocator changes that exercises churny session profiles before broad rollout.

Miscellaneous smaller items (housekeeping)
- Samir: will schedule the allocator sim cluster time (requesting 2x 8h windows for Dec 2-3).
- Lena: cleaning up old cache metrics to reduce cardinality; will submit metric removal PR.
- Jules: prepping a one-pager for the PM to justify adding a permanent fallback-alert and associated oncall rota change.

Notes to self (Maya):
- Draft the postmortem skeleton tonight and share with the group tomorrow. Keep the timeline tight and include the mitigations we used as timeline markers.

If you have follow-ups or additional traces please paste into PLT-4821 thread. Will reconvene in two days for status and to review the allocator sim results.

-- end of workbench standup notes (informal)
